context.instructions: Read input/, your workspace and, through record_map.read_tool, the records of the input snapshot that record_map allows. Pass the exact absolute workspace as workdir on every shell call, with login=false. Use absolute paths under this workspace for file reads and writes; a shell's default working directory may differ. Ask for missing inputs. Never read other runs' workspaces or the central repository directly. New research source code belongs in this workspace.

scholarly.availability: Confirm the tools actually exposed in this execution; configuration is not a successful call.

knowledge.meaning: A stated mathematical or research definition.
A proposition proposed for formal and semantic verification.
A bounded observation with stated evidence and scope.
A recorded obstruction or failed approach.
A proposed definition not yet adopted.
A proposed proof or proof direction.
A result whose verified scope is smaller than the target.

relations.meaning: Research evidence supports consideration; it does not imply the target.
Research evidence challenges a claim without itself refuting it.
The target was generated from the source.
The target is a newer meaning-preserving or explicitly revised record.
The target was derived using the source as research input.
The source cites the target as evidence or background.
The target refines the source as a research judgment, not a formal implication.
The target is one part split from the source.
The records are analogous in the stated respects; no implication is asserted.
The source establishes the target problem in the stated scope.
The source formally refutes the target claim.
The source formally addresses an explicit part of the target.
The source formally justifies a narrower target scope.
The source proposition formally implies the target proposition.
The source and target are formally equivalent in both directions.
The source problem formally reduces to the target problem.
The source is formally encoded by the target with stated preservation.
The target formally simulates the stated source behavior.

rules: Use only assigned inputs, allowed queries and your execution workspace.
Do not read other reviewers' private work or modify central records directly.
Deliver proposals as a normal JSON final, or use the supplied tools for optional early submission.
Do not issue user controls or expand research goals, budgets or external authority.

role_review.source_instructions: Read each referenced source through its local_path when needed. The JSON file contains the exact original public message; its content is the original source body. Compare the complete current proposal. Prior revision judgments do not approve this revision.

item.question: One fixed question to investigate
source_refs: proposal or proposal:<field.path>, issue:<id>, supplied source ref, or readable knowledge ID

research_request_contract.instructions: If investigation is necessary, write research_requests and return unresolved provisionally for initial/judge. The slot is deferred without sealing a verdict; all requested answers return to this same slot. Use an existing answer when it resolves the question. Investigation cannot replace your final complete review.

execution_window.instruction: Read management notices under .control after start. A finish request asks for normal submission and does not revoke authority.

record_map.instruction: record_index lists by storage family the IDs of the input snapshot records this role may read and cite. Read a record, or a file of this snapshot, with read_tool; cite a record by its ID. ledger=supplied_only: this independent judgment reads the research canon, except a root/family in blocked_keys, and only the execution-ledger (runtime/) records its input supplies.
